author: Ruben Hassid
basis: First-person process account; article disclosed as AI-generated
reported_outcomes: Reports making a preference file after an interview and finding its output closer to his style; no independent voice or thinking test.
proposed_outcomes: Make writing preferences explicit enough to use and revise.
limits: A text profile is not a person, identity or complete thinking process.
The demand for exactly 100 questions and pressure not to accept uncertainty are not validated requirements.
Removing hedging as a style rule must not erase evidential uncertainty.
review_note: Retain an example-based preference interview; reject the central claim that reproducing style duplicates a person.
coverage: Close-read all 594 lines of available extracted article text; image-only content and linked media not reviewed.
